# Skeleton Loading Pattern

## Why Skeletons

Skeleton screens show the layout before data arrives. They reduce perceived wait time compared to blank screens or spinners — the user sees structure immediately.

Use skeletons for:
- Lists and tables that take > 300ms to load
- Dashboard cards with metrics
- Profile sections

Use a simple spinner for:
- Button actions (< 2s expected)
- Full-page transitions (paired with loading.tsx)

## shadcn/ui Skeleton Component

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add skeleton
```

```typescript
// components/ui/skeleton.tsx (auto-generated by shadcn)
// Uses: animate-pulse + rounded-md bg-muted
```

## Skeleton Patterns

### Table Skeleton
```typescript
// components/InvoiceTableSkeleton.tsx
import { Skeleton } from '@/components/ui/skeleton'

export function InvoiceTableSkeleton({ rows = 5 }: { rows?: number }) {
  return (
    <div className="space-y-2">
      {/* Header */}
      <div className="flex gap-4 pb-2 border-b">
        <Skeleton className="h-4 w-24" />
        <Skeleton className="h-4 w-32" />
        <Skeleton className="h-4 w-20 ml-auto" />
      </div>
      {/* Rows */}
      {Array.from({ length: rows }).map((_, i) => (
        <div key={i} className="flex gap-4 py-2">
          <Skeleton className="h-4 w-24" />
          <Skeleton className="h-4 w-48" />
          <Skeleton className="h-4 w-16 ml-auto" />
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Card Skeleton
```typescript
export function StatCardSkeleton() {
  return (
    <div className="p-4 border rounded-lg space-y-2">
      <Skeleton className="h-3 w-20" />      {/* label */}
      <Skeleton className="h-8 w-16" />       {/* value */}
      <Skeleton className="h-3 w-32" />       {/* subtitle */}
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Profile Skeleton
```typescript
export function ProfileSkeleton() {
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-4">
      <Skeleton className="h-12 w-12 rounded-full" />  {/* avatar */}
      <div className="space-y-2">
        <Skeleton className="h-4 w-32" />   {/* name */}
        <Skeleton className="h-3 w-24" />   {/* email */}
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Using Skeletons with Suspense

```typescript
// Streaming with Suspense — skeleton shows while server component loads
import { Suspense } from 'react'
import { InvoiceTable } from './InvoiceTable'
import { InvoiceTableSkeleton } from './InvoiceTableSkeleton'

export default function InvoicesPage() {
  return (
    <div>
      <h1>Invoices</h1>
      <Suspense fallback={<InvoiceTableSkeleton rows={10} />}>
        <InvoiceTable />  {/* async Server Component */}
      </Suspense>
    </div>
  )
}
```

The Server Component that actually fetches data:
```typescript
// async Server Component — suspends while fetching
async function InvoiceTable() {
  const invoices = await fetchInvoices()  // suspends here
  return <Table data={invoices} />
}
```

## Using Skeletons with loading.tsx

```typescript
// app/(portal)/invoices/loading.tsx
// This automatically shows while the page.tsx Server Component loads
import { InvoiceTableSkeleton } from '@/components/InvoiceTableSkeleton'
import { Skeleton } from '@/components/ui/skeleton'

export default function InvoicesLoading() {
  return (
    <div className="space-y-6">
      <div className="flex justify-between">
        <Skeleton className="h-8 w-32" />    {/* page title */}
        <Skeleton className="h-9 w-28" />    {/* action button */}
      </div>
      <InvoiceTableSkeleton rows={8} />
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Making Skeletons Match Real Content

The skeleton should closely mirror the actual layout — same heights, same column proportions. A skeleton that looks nothing like the actual content causes jarring layout shift when data arrives.

Match:
- Column widths (proportionally)
- Row heights
- Number of items shown (use a reasonable estimate)
- Any badges or chips (show as small rounded rectangles)

Don't try to be perfect — close enough prevents jarring shifts.
